assessment.governing_intent: Prove the SWF-27 observer replacement gate for R4 by demonstrating no observation loss across the boundary, preserving consumer identity/order/timestamps/anomalies/retention across restart and attention-producer consumption, and retaining the attention queue even if the observer is later retired, without performing live retirement or broadening scope.
implementation_unknowns: Whether the pinned FX-R4 fixture fully specifies executable commands, inputs, expected outcomes, and evidence schema sufficient for the R4 predicate.
How the implementation will collect and retain immutable evidence receipts, raw observations, negative controls, command/exit status, and independent verdicts in the required format.

Whether the existing observer/store/harness interfaces already expose the needed restart, interruption, restoration, generation-contrast, consumer, identity, retention, and attention-queue checks without code changes.
How applicability revisions, authority/source-change observations, and conservative holds are represented in the existing system during guarded admission.
How to verify preservation of the attention queue while avoiding any unauthorized live cutover or retirement claim.
material_risks: Proceeding without the required FX-R4 operational execution would produce only a local or preparatory result and would not satisfy the R4 acceptance predicate.
The predecessor B1 proof is reported as explicitly scoped not to discharge R4's own no-loss/cutover-reconciliation and attention-queue-retention predicate.
Unauthorized cutover, retirement, release, or production-scope change would violate the stated retirement-gate boundary.
Missing or unavailable measurements must be treated as holds, not PASS or zero, creating a hard evidence risk if the operational target or readback is unavailable.
Candidate custody requirements require exact branch/SHA, independently retrieved verifier worktree, retained receipts, and no direct main push; absent custody artifacts would block acceptance.
If FX-R4 uses disposable fixture state without a separately authorized operational target/readback, it may fail to meet the OPERATIONAL_OR_EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY proof level.
assessment.next_action: Hold until the required execution supply is available: identify and authorize the operational target/profile for FX-R4, execute the pinned fixture under the required custody rules, retain the full evidence package and independent verdict, then reassess the exact resulting revision.
assessment.rationale: The controlling condition is not ambiguous product intent and not multiple independent decision centers; it is unavailable prerequisite proof/execution supply. The task text itself says the authority delegation does not bind the BIU's own required operational target, no FX-R4 execution record exists, operational fixtures require their separately authorized target and actual readback, TASKS is not READY, and proof/custody gates remain required before READY. Those statements establish a HOLD until the external operational proof and evidence prerequisites exist.
assessment.summary: The task has coherent intent and a bounded node scope, but the supplied text establishes that required proof/custody/execution gates are not yet satisfied. Authority gates are reported as disposed for Wave 2, and FX-R4 preparation is reported as pinned, but the text also states that no FX-R4 execution record exists, the operational target/proof still must be supplied, TASKS is not READY, and all dependency/authority/proof/custody gates remain required before READY. This is therefore blocked on external execution/proof supply rather than unclear owner intent or a need to split the work.
assessment.verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable in principle: FX-R4 must show no observation loss across the boundary, continuity of consumer/identity/restart/retention behavior, retained attention queue, and discriminating intact/fault/restored controls, with exact fixture/source/profile/candidate revisions, invocation, command, expected/observed result, exit status, immutable observation refs, and an independent verdict where required. One independent verdict would be meaningful because the node has a single governing proof predicate. However, the supplied text reports that the operational proof has not yet been executed and that local substitutions cannot satisfy operational acceptance.
